mechanism.statement: Let every durable semantic bit available to recovery live inside one rollback/delete-recreate authority domain D. Let D be restorable byte-for-byte to ancestor state S0 while erasing all later in-domain refs, receipts, nonces, epochs, journals and semantic copies associated with later state S1. After that restoration, the recovery observation is identical in world A, where S1 existed and was erased, and world B, where S1 never existed. Any recovery algorithm restricted to D therefore receives the same input in A and B and cannot both reconstruct the particular erased S1 in A and avoid fabricating S1 in B. Randomization does not restore information absent from the observation; it can only guess.
mechanism.consequence: Sound recovery across complete same-domain rewind requires at least one durable witness outside the rewindable authority domain, or else fail-closed non-recovery. An out-of-domain witness is not accepted merely by existing: it must separately satisfy zero residual Work/protected-primary/manual-user execution, zero finite monthly/trial/paid quota dependency, zero incremental monetary cost, exact provenance and safe automatic continuation.
distinction_from_prior_exact_mechanisms: Distinct from CURRENT-REACHABLE-ROLE-SEMANTIC-COPY-WITH-FAIL-CLOSED-GC-BOUNDARY-v1 because that method protects information only while a current reachable copy survives inside D; this bound covers deletion/rewind of all such in-domain copies.
Distinct from AT-LEAST-ONE-RANDOM-NONCE-ATTEMPT-WITNESS-v1 because a nonce witness stored only in D is erased by the assumed complete rewind and cannot distinguish worlds A and B afterward.
Distinct from membership-epoch/shared-CAS mechanisms because stronger in-domain ordering metadata is still erased when every witness in D is restored to S0.
